title: certeza: Scientific Framework for Asymptotic Test Effectiveness in Rust
description: A research framework for approaching practical maximum confidence in software testing through tiered verification, property-based testing, mutation analysis, and scientific performance benchmarking. Includes comprehensive specifications (~26.5K words), Rust implementation with PMAT compliance, and reproducible benchmarking infrastructure.
references: Dijkstra, E. W. (1972). Notes On Structured Programming. Structured Programming.
Claessen, K., & Hughes, J. (2000). QuickCheck: A Lightweight Tool for Random Testing of Haskell Programs. ICFP.
Jia, Y., & Harman, M. (2011). An Analysis and Survey of the Development of Mutation Testing. IEEE TSE.
Chen, T. Y., Kuo, F.-C., & Zhou, Z. Q. (2018). Metamorphic Testing: A New Approach for Generating Next Test Cases. HKUST Tech Report.
Fleming, P. J., & Wallace, J. J. (1986). How not to lie with statistics: The correct way to summarize benchmark results. CACM.
notes:
This archive includes:

1. Complete source code (Rust implementation)
2. Comprehensive specifications:
   - Asymptotic Test Effectiveness Framework (v1.1, ~14K words)
   - Scientific Reporting and Benchmarking Framework (v1.0, ~12.5K words)
3. Benchmarking infrastructure:
   - TypeScript/Deno reporting tools
   - Statistical analysis utilities
   - Multi-format report generators (JSON, CSV, Markdown, HTML)
4. PMAT-compliant quality gates and CI/CD configuration
5. Reproducibility artifacts:
   - Dockerfile for hermetic builds
   - Toolchain manifests
   - Validation scripts
6. Example benchmark results and reports

Reproduction Instructions:
See REPRODUCTION.md for step-by-step instructions to reproduce all results from scratch using Docker or native builds.

System Requirements:
- Rust 1.82.0 (pinned via rust-toolchain.toml)
- Deno 2.x (for reporting scripts)
- Docker (optional, for hermetic builds)
